issues.problem: No evidence yet that the count reaches B at step ~15000; smoke runs stop at 2000 (0.72M vs target 1.24M, every candidate already cloned/split). The 2000-step shortfall is candidate-limited exactly like official densify_with_score, not a bug.
issues.evidence: official: budget=min(budget, n_clone+n_split+curr); clone/split budgets proportional; all candidates sampled when budget >= candidates. Plugin core.split_budgets/densify identical; smoke log shows clones==clone_candidates, splits==split_candidates at every call 600..2000. Candidate rate ~7-14% of N per call; target slope 77k*(1-c/145) per call decays to ~0, so the gap closes around call 25-35 (N~0.9-1.2M) and N tracks the curve afterwards (late cands ~5% of N >> slope).
issues.fix: Before the full benchmark, run garden to step ~6000-8000 (or watch history rows) and check count >= 0.98*target by call ~40; consider a train-log warning when count < 0.95*target after call 60.

issues.problem: Taming candidates run 2-27% below the stock gsplat baseline in the same smoke (148.6k vs 145.9k at 600, 292k vs 269k at 1000, 844k vs 717k at 2000) although the candidate rule/threshold/accumulation are identical to gsplat DefaultStrategy.
issues.evidence: Only differences are shN lr 2.5e-4 + 16-step batching, opacity lr 0.025 and score-guided sampling (picks all candidates anyway). Plausibly an optimization-trajectory effect, not verified.
issues.fix: Optional: A/B with sh_update_every=1 for 2000 steps to confirm the lag is the SH change; no code change required.

issues.problem: Runtime steps optimizers before after_backward, so opacity receives the step-15000 Adam update before the lr=0 freeze; official freezes before the step-15000 update (the update goes to the orphaned old Parameter).
issues.evidence: runtime.py: opt.step() then density.after_backward; train.py: modify_functions() then optimizer.step().
issues.fix: Negligible (one step); note in plan gaps (already covered by gap 4 in spirit).

issues.problem: Edge map input is round()ed uint8; official get_edges uses ToPILImage on float -> mul(255).byte() (truncation). Also SH degree for the score render at step k*1000 is k-1 (runtime) vs k (official oneupSHdegree at the start of that iteration).
issues.evidence: taming_utils.get_edges; train.py line 96-97 vs runtime.py degree=min((step-1)//1000,3).
issues.fix: Optional: truncate instead of round when caching; effect on scores negligible.

summary: No critical or major issues. The 0.72M vs 1.24M shortfall at step 2000 is faithful to official densify_with_score: the target is only an upper cap, min(target, candidates+current), and every candidate was already used. Growth should catch the decaying parabola by call ~30 and reach B at the end, but this is analytical; confirm with a longer garden run before the full benchmark.
